summary: AttnCompress is a middleware for SE agents (implemented in Trae-Agent) that compresses past trajectory turns by segmenting observations at perplexity spikes, scoring blocks with a small proxy model's attention to the agent's current reasoning, and re-evaluating suppressed blocks via a rolling window. It is compared with seven compression baselines on a 200-instance SWE-bench Verified test split (three agent LLMs) and on 300-instance Multi-SWE-Bench-Flash (seven languages including Java).

claims.claim: AttnCompress achieves a 53.17% pass rate, outperforming prior SOTA compression baselines.
claims.evidence: Table 1: 53.17% is the mean across Gemini-3-Flash (71.50), Qwen3-235B (43.50), Qwen3-Coder-30B (44.50) vs AgentDiet 51.17, LLMSummary 50.83, SlidingWindow 49.83; it is below the uncompressed Original (55.17). Table 2 (5 runs, Qwen3-Coder-30B): AttnCompress 43.70 +/- 2.17 vs LLMSummary 42.70 +/- 2.22, AgentDiet 41.80 +/- 2.99, Original 44.10 +/- 2.38, so gaps to the best baselines are within one SD.

claims.claim: Token consumption falls 21.6% and total cost 33.6%.
claims.evidence: Both percentages are relative to AgentDiet (input 644.66k vs 822.44k; cost $0.0949 vs $0.1429), a baseline that is itself costlier than no compression ($0.1189). Against Original, input -42.3% and cost -20.2%. ObsMask is far cheaper ($0.0443, input 628.93k) at -6 pp pass rate. Numbers verified in Table 1/§5.1.

claims.claim: Each component (PPL segmentation, proxy attention, rolling window) is essential.
claims.evidence: Table 3 on the 100-instance validation set, single run: full 42.0 vs w/o PPL 39.0, w/o attention 35.0, w/o rolling 37.0. Differences of 3-7 instances on n=100, against ~2.2 pp run-to-run SD measured on n=200.

claims.claim: The framework is model-agnostic and generalises across languages.
claims.evidence: Table 7 (Multi-SWE-Bench-Flash, 300 instances): 19.67% vs Original 20.33%, AgentDiet 18.33%; Java 17 passed, equal to Original vs AgentDiet 13 (Fig. 5). Single run, per-language differences of 0-4 instances. Only one agent framework (Trae-Agent) tested (§6).

patterns.note: Every compression method, including AttnCompress, lowers pass rate vs full context (Table 1, Table 7); AttnCompress loses least and cuts cost ~20% vs Original, while cheap ObsMask halves cost at a larger accuracy loss.
Reports per-instance tokens, agent vs compression cost with prefix-caching discounts, and latency breakdown; shows LLM-summary compression (AgentDiet) can cost more than no compression.
Uses a small proxy model (Qwen3-4B class; Llama/Gemma variants tested) for relevance scoring beside a larger agent model.
Evaluated only on SWE-bench Verified subset and Multi-SWE-Bench-Flash.

methodology.sample: SWE-bench Verified: AgentDiet's 100-instance validation split (tuning/ablation) and 200-instance test split; Multi-SWE-Bench-Flash: 300 instances in 7 languages.
methodology.baselines: Original (full context), Random, SlidingWindow (8k), ObsMask, LLMLingua, LLMSummary, AgentDiet, all re-run inside Trae-Agent with tail size k=2 and default hyperparameters; no tuning of baselines reported.
methodology.models: Agent LLMs: Gemini-3-Flash, Qwen3-235B-Instruct, Qwen3-Coder-30B; proxy models Qwen, Llama-3.2-3B, Gemma-3-4B.
methodology.variance: Five repeated runs only for Qwen3-Coder-30B on SWE-bench Verified (Table 2); everything else single-run.
methodology.ablations: Component ablation and five-hyperparameter sensitivity on the validation split (Tables 3-4).
methodology.contamination_controls: Acknowledged SWE-bench leakage risk; argues relative comparisons unaffected and adds Multi-SWE-Bench (§6).
methodology.languages: Python (SWE-bench Verified); C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Rust, TypeScript (Multi-SWE-Bench-Flash).

standards.artifacts: Replication package with source and scripts at github.com/ZZR0/AttnCompress (Data Availability).

biases.detail: Abstract presents 53.17% as SOTA without saying it is a three-model mean below the no-compression baseline; 'strictly preserve critical task evidence' contradicts the failure analysis that it drops later-needed file paths and errors.
Headline 21.6% token / 33.6% cost reductions are measured against AgentDiet, the most expensive baseline, rather than against Original or the cheapest competitive baseline.
Multi-model, multi-language and ablation results are single runs; the one repeated-run table shows differences within SD.
Ablation deltas are 3-7 instances on a 100-instance split; per-language Multi-SWE results differ by 0-4 instances.
Validation/test splits and protocol inherited from AgentDiet on SWE-bench Verified; only one agent framework (Trae-Agent).
Authors re-implement all baselines in their harness with default settings.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None owned by authors; third-party Gemini and Qwen models.

verdict_reason: Peer-reviewed, released, three agent models, seven baselines, held-out split and a five-run robustness check, but the advantage over the best baselines is within run-to-run noise, the method still loses to full context, and the headline cost reductions are framed against the costliest baseline.
applicability: Moderately relevant to the harness cost question. For a Java team running long ingestion-pipeline debugging sessions across >=4 repositories, the paper's numbers say: (a) full context remains the accuracy ceiling, so compress only when context limits or cost force it; (b) LLM-summary compression can cost more than not compressing; (c) cheap rule-based masking of old tool outputs (ObsMask) roughly halves cost with a few points lost, which is the easiest host-neutral option. The Java subset (Multi-SWE-Bench-Flash, 17 passed vs 17 Original) is too small to conclude much. AttnCompress needs a proxy model in the request path and integration inside the agent loop, which most commercial agent hosts (mixed host setup) do not expose, and it has no bearing on spec-driven development or healthcare content.

conflicts_with.detail: FOCUS reports compression improving task success by up to 8.9 points over uncompressed execution (non-SE agent tasks), whereas here every compression method, including AttnCompress, underperforms full context on SWE tasks.
Implicit (embedding) compression sharply reduced SWE-bench resolution; AttnCompress's explicit block selection loses only ~2 pp, suggesting the compression form matters more than compression per se.
